name: Sanctify
dek: An analytics dashboard and the system behind it: Catholic values screening made inspectable.

at_a_glance.role: Sole UX/UI designer, end to end
at_a_glance.scope: Competitor analysis, user flows, design system, marketing site, two dashboards, mobile app
at_a_glance.hard_part: Making a moral screening score feel trustworthy meant showing its math: every rating breaks down into named categories with visible sub-scores.
at_a_glance.look_for: How one component language, rating rings, score bars, sector charts, holds together across the marketing site, both dashboards, and the app.

problem.claim_h2: Ethical screening tools hide the one thing users came for
problem.thesis: An investor who wants a portfolio aligned with Catholic teaching has no simple way to see why any company passes or fails.
problem.body: Sanctify is a screening platform that rates companies against Catholic moral categories, with a marketing site, a user dashboard, an admin dashboard, and a mobile app. The design problem was less about charts and more about trust: the score only works if its reasoning is visible.
bullets: Faith-based competitors keep their screening methodology opaque, so users cannot verify the rating.
Most tools show no dashboard preview before signup and little data visualization once inside.
Financial products bury non-professional investors in jargon and complexity.
problem.research_note: Desk research compared Inspire Investing, Eventide, and GuideStone Funds on messaging, transparency, and data visualization, which surfaced the pain points above.

design.claim_h2: Show the score's work, everywhere the score appears
design.intro: One green-led component language carries the moral rating from the first marketing touch to the deepest dashboard card.

figures.caption: The hero pairs the value proposition with a full trial signup form, so conversion starts before any scrolling.
figures.alt: Sanctify homepage hero: dark navy background, white headline about Catholic values investing, and a white 14-day free trial signup form with name, email, company, and phone fields.

figures.caption: Real dashboard components on the marketing page preview the product before signup, a gap every competitor left open.
figures.alt: Marketing section showing dashboard previews: an AA score ring, a sector breakdown bar chart, a market value card, and a checklist of screening categories like Banking and Lending and Gambling.

figures.caption: The user dashboard breaks the rating into letter-graded categories with per-screen percentage bars, so the number is inspectable.
figures.alt: User dashboard with metric cards, an Add Screenset form, category cards graded A to D for Adult Content, Environment, and others, sector breakdown and performance charts, and notes and changes panels.

figures.caption: The admin view swaps moral detail for oversight: user trends, a pass and fail donut of screened companies, and a managed user table.
figures.alt: Admin dashboard with user metrics, a yearly users line chart, a pass and fail company statistic donut, a recent users table with a row action menu, and activity log panels.

figures.caption: Mobile auth stays minimal, two fields to log in, five to sign up, with the brand's green reserved for the single primary action.
figures.alt: Two iPhone screens on black: a Sanctify login screen with email and password fields and a green Log In button, and a sign up screen with name, business email, company, and phone fields.

validation.honest_line: Testing was scoped to task scenarios walked through on the hi-fi prototype, enough to check navigation and hierarchy, not enough to claim validated behavior with real investors.

appendix.framing: The flows and component sheet show how four surfaces stayed coherent. Every screen above is assembled from this one kit.

figures.caption: Three user-story flows, investor screening, admin user creation, and visitor conversion, mapped before any UI was drawn.
figures.alt: Flowchart diagrams on black for three user stories: adding a screen set from the dashboard, an admin adding a user by invitation or manually, and a visitor moving from homepage to signup.

figures.caption: The shared kit: charts, score bars, dropdowns, steppers, and every navigation state for both the app and the marketing site.
figures.alt: Component sheet showing sector breakdown charts, dropdowns, pagination, checkboxes, toggles, score bars, a performance chart, seven dashboard navigation bar states, report summary tabs, and five marketing site navbar states.
